to click add personal statement, we need to edit that, and then we can select citations, for positions ,scientific appointments and honors, we can add those by clicking here, And we can add the honors by clicking here and for contributions to science we can fill that out by clicking here. All right, just to save some time I'm going to go with an NIH biosketch I've already partially filled out. So we have we have the name; if I want to link it to an ERA Commons account I can click that. For education and training I have one entry, so let's go ahead and add another degree and training. So this is a degree, and I'll just fill this out. All right so I've filled out the information, and I will click save and add another entry because I have to put in my bachelor's degree, or if that was my last degree I could just click save. Okay so I've filled in all my education and training and I have entered a personal statement. This personal statement is short because in my previous video I talked about what to put in the personal statement. In this video I'm just showing you how to use the software. So we have a short personal statement here, and we can select some citations to add to it as is allowed. So I'm just going to go to my oldest ones and select four. For the purposes of this video I'm not putting a lot of thought into which citations I'm going to add here. When you do your biosketch, do put a lot of thought into it. All right so once you have selected the citations go up here and say save citations. So now those will appear with my personal statement. Next we have positions and scientific appointments, so I have listed some of my positions back to 2008, but I'm going to add one more entry to show you how this works. So I'll go to edit entries, and then add another entry. So I've filled in the information and I click save. Let's add some honors here. So I'll just add one honor, and we'll save that. And if you want to add additional ones just click add another entry. Then we'll move to the contributions to science section. And you can see I've already added one, with my description and citations. So let's say edit this section, and I will add another contribution. So for the description I need to say edit, and then I'll paste in my text, and then click the green check mark to save it. And then select the citations that I want to designate as relevant to this contribution. So I've selected four citations here and I'm going to save citations. And do I want to include a link to the complete list of published work in My Bibliography, yes, so I have checked this box. It shows the link here. So that's it, I'm done. So what I can do now is download this biosketch, and I can do that as a PDF, as a Word document, or as an XML. So I'm going to go with the PDF because that's what I need to submit to NIH. So I click PDF, it prepares my file for download, downloads. Let's open it. And there it is. Okay so it's all filled out. We have my name, my title, my education, training, my personal statement, positions, specific appointments, and honors, contributions to science; I just have two of them and each of those has four citations. And then a complete list to my published work. So that's a really easy way to make your biosketch with this software and to customize it each time you make a new biosketch for a different application. I hope that was helpful to you. If you have any questions you can leave them in the comments below. If you got value from this video please hit the like button and consider subscribing to the Grants and Publications YouTube channel for more information and tips about scientific writing related topics. Thanks for watching. I'll see you next time and happy writing!
